reason: E1 directly supports the premise that kinetic effects overcompensate thermodynamic contributions in dissolution, but it does not address surface diffusion or encapsulating layers. E2 demonstrates synthesis of graphene-encapsulated HEA nanoparticles but provides no evidence on their stability or diffusion kinetics under operating conditions. The core mechanistic claims about surface diffusion and kinetic barriers are therefore largely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Thermodynamic stabilization alone does not ensure high-entropy alloy nanoparticle stability under operating conditions
Kinetic limitations on surface atomic diffusion are the primary control on structural/chemical stability
An encapsulating layer can act as a surface kinetic barrier to slow atomic rearrangements and dissolution
Without a kinetic barrier, nanoparticles will exhibit faster elemental segregation and degradation at high temperatures
